jurisdiction.name: Namibia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Namibia has no AI law, no adopted AI strategy and no AI guidance from any regulator. Its only official AI-governance document found online is the 2022 final report of the Presidential Task Force on the Fourth Industrial Revolution, which recommends a National AI Institute. A national AI strategy led by the National Commission on Research, Science and Technology, an AI bill, a data protection bill and a cybercrime bill are all still in preparation.
lead_institutions: National Commission on Research, Science and Technology (NCRST)
Ministry of Information and Communication Technology
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but the ICT ministry's, Parliament's, the government portal's and the planning commission's websites could not be accessed, and the gazette pages could only be seen in search results. Only one document could be read, so Namibia is marked for a later retry. The planned AI strategy, AI bill, data protection bill and digital strategy are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Task Force on the Fourth Industrial Revolution: “4IR as an Enabler of Green and Inclusive Industrialisation” – Final Report
instruments.english_title: Presidential Task Force on the Fourth Industrial Revolution: Final Report – "4IR as an Enabler of Green and Inclusive Industrialisation"
instruments.issuing_authority: Task Force on the Fourth Industrial Revolution (appointed by the President of Namibia), supported by the Office of the Prime Minister, the Ministry of Labour, Industrial Relations and Employment Creation and the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology
instruments.current_status: Final report submitted to the President in August 2022 and published by NCRST on its Downloads page. Its recommendations are not binding. Official statements in 2025-2026 report that NCRST set up a national AI working group following the Task Force's recommendation and is leading consultations on a national AI strategy, which had not been published as of October 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Final report of the eight-member Task Force on the Fourth Industrial Revolution, appointed by President Hage Geingob and serving from 1 July 2021 to 30 June 2022, assessing Namibia's readiness for 4IR technologies (including AI) through a Country 4IR Readiness Assessment Framework, a WEF Future of Production benchmark and a survey with 514 responses. It makes 13 recommendations, including a consolidated national 4IR strategy, a National 4IR Commission, a comprehensive policy and legislative review, prioritising cybersecurity, and (Recommendation 13) a National AI Institute to coordinate AI R&D, promote trustworthy, ethical and responsible AI in the public and private sectors and coordinate AI activities across government agencies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Namibia's first government-commissioned AI/4IR readiness assessment; source of the recommendation for a national AI institute and the NCRST-led AI strategy work.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Namibia's gazettes and legislation, parliament, the research council, ministries and regulators were searched. No AI law or national AI strategy has been published, and no AI material was found in the other categories; AI, data protection and cybercrime bills are listed as leads. The websites of the information and communications technology ministry, parliament, the government portal and the planning commission were unavailable, so the national digital strategy, the national development plan and the data protection bill's status remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. mict.gov.na reset/503; parliament.na, gov.na reset; npc.gov.na TLS/503; opm.gov.na proxy 502; NamibLII gazette pages 403 (snippets only). Gazette No. 8954 (19 Jun 2026) ICT standard mentions AI in passing - not recorded. Secondary claims of a Feb 2025 strategy launch contradicted by ministers' statements (lead). BoN Fintech Innovation Regulatory Framework 2026 read: no AI. MICT org name unverified. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: NamibLII full-text search of gazettes and legislation for 'artificial intelligence': no AI law or AI provisions; hits were qualification registrations (Bachelor of AI, 2025), trademark classes, CRAN 5G/IMT strategy (2023) and a June 2026 gazette (No. 8954) cyber standard mentioning AI-driven technologies only in passing. AI Bill, Data Protection Bill and Cybercrime Bill unpublished -> leads. parliament.na unreachable.; Government: NCRST (publications/downloads): 4IR Task Force Final Report (recorded). National AI strategy: not published (lead). MICT National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 and NPC NDP6: official sites unreachable (leads).; Ministries: Education, health, justice, defence, finance, labour, home affairs: searched, nothing found (education digital teaching and learning policy draft -> lead).; Regulators: Bank of Namibia: Fintech Innovation Regulatory Framework (2026) read, contains no AI provisions; AI media release only (lab funding). CRAN: blog articles on AI attacks and sandboxes only (sandbox framework -> lead). NAMFISA: no AI-specific standard found. No data protection authority exists yet.. Not reached: mict.gov.na (connection reset; WebFetch HTTP 503); parliament.na (connection reset); gov.na (connection reset); npc.gov.na (TLS failure; WebFetch HTTP 503); opm.gov.na (proxy 502); NamibLII gazette pages (HTTP 403) - only search snippets read. Could not verify: National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 (mict.gov.na unreachable); NDP6 (npc.gov.na unreachable); Data Protection Bill tabling status (parliament.na unreachable). binding-law, strategy, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (in preparation)
leads.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Namibia
leads.issuing_authority: National Commission on Research, Science and Technology / Ministry of Information and Communication Technology
leads.note: Ministers stated in 2025-2026 that Namibia has no adopted national AI strategy yet and that NCRST is leading consultations on an AI Strategy Framework (reportedly with Deloitte). Some secondary sources claim a strategy was 'launched' in February 2025; no official text found on ncrst.na or mict.gov.na (MICT site unreachable). Record as national_strategy once an official text is published.
